newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: U.K. doctor gets suspended sentence over NZ death.
newsitem.headline: U.K. doctor gets suspended sentence over NZ death.

text.p: A New Zealand judge imposed a six-month suspended sentence on British surgeon Keith Ramstead on Friday over the death of an elderly woman patient on the operating table.
Justice Anthony Ellis upheld Ramstead's conviction over the death of Nancie Muncie after a jury last week found him guilty of her manslaughter.
Ellis said he was satisfied there had been a serious lapse on Ramstead's part, but the sentence took into account the ordeal the surgeon had experienced.
"What you have suffered has been extreme," Ellis said.
The suspended sentence means Ramstead could be jailed if he reoffended within the six-month period.

The 44-year-old surgeon was found not guilty of the manslaughter of two male patients, aged 50 and 74, who also died during operations he performed while working at a Christchurch hospital in 1991 and 1992.
The jury of six men and six women deliberated for 24 hours, spread over three days before reaching their verdict last Thursday.
